domain: Structural Dynamics of Agency Depletion / Social Constraint Theory / Power Asymmetry
topic_summary: Analysis of constraint dynamics where identical structural rules produce radically different experiential outcomes based on power position, exit options, and time horizons. The formalization demonstrates how natural law (mountains), social stigma (indexically variable), and relational obligations (degrading purity) interact to create extraction traps for the powerless while functioning as coordination mechanisms for the powerful.

key_entities: Powerless agent (π=1.5, immediate horizon, trapped exit condition)
Powerful agent (π=0.6, biographical horizon, mobile exit condition)
Dependent agent (π=1.5, biographical horizon, constrained exit condition)
key_tensions: Indexical variance: same constraint experienced as coordination (Rope) by powerful vs extraction (Snare) by powerless
Purity drift: legitimate reciprocal obligations degrade into pure extraction as coordination function atrophies
False mountain naturalization: socially constructed constraints misclassified as immutable natural law by those trapped within them

axes.structural_delta: Identical enforcement mechanism produces coordination for powerful agents and extraction for powerless agents based solely on index position (power, time horizon, exit options)
axes.primary_observable: χ variance across agents for same constraint; ratio of coordination benefit to extraction cost as function of power position
axes.selection_reason: Highest centrality; core mechanism explaining how same rule = different realities; upstream to both other dynamics

axes.human_readable: False Mountain Naturalization (Misclassification of Changeable as Immutable)
axes.structural_delta: Agents trapped in high-extraction positions misclassify socially constructed constraints as natural law, wasting agency on acceptance rather than transformation
axes.primary_observable: Type I error rate (treating ε>0.15 as ε=0.0); verbal naturalization patterns; behavioral resignation despite available collective action
axes.selection_reason: Downstream synthesis of indexical asymmetry; distinct observable (cognitive misclassification vs structural position); high ε difference from axis 1

axes.human_readable: Purity Drift Degradation (Entropic Decay of Reciprocal Obligations)
axes.structural_delta: Legitimate reciprocal obligations naturally degrade over time as coordination function atrophies while extraction persists, transforming tangled ropes into snares without policy change
axes.primary_observable: Purity metric P(t) = coordination_value / (coordination_value + extraction_cost) declining below 0.40 threshold; behavioral shift from mutual benefit to unilateral burden
axes.selection_reason: Downstream synthesis; distinct mechanism (temporal degradation vs static position); captures dynamic transformation absent from other axes

axes.human_readable: Network Contamination Cascade (Snare Infection of Rope Systems)
axes.structural_delta: High-extraction constraints contaminate adjacent coordination systems through enforcement spillover, causing intrinsically healthy ropes to reproduce extraction patterns
axes.primary_observable: Purity decline in focal system correlated with enforcement intensity of adjacent snare; internalization of stigma within mutual aid structures
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: lower centrality than selected axes; network dynamics captured indirectly via indexical asymmetry + purity drift interaction

axes.human_readable: Collective Action Threshold (Coordination Escape from Snare)
axes.structural_delta: Organized collective action transforms snares into ropes by shifting power index from powerless (π=1.5) to organized (π=0.4), but requires critical mass and coordination costs
axes.primary_observable: χ transformation via power shift; minimum group size for successful transformation; coordination cost vs extraction reduction trade-off
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: scaffold type (intervention mechanism not structural constraint); counterfactual rather than observed dynamic

deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Lower centrality; network dynamics emerge from interaction of selected axes rather than requiring independent treatment

omegas.description: How are power (π), time horizon (T), and exit condition (E) operationalized for empirical measurement? Index values in formalization are illustrative; real-world application requires validated instruments.
Are χ thresholds (Rope <0.46, Tangled 0.46-0.76, Snare >0.66) universal or domain-dependent? Formalization uses fixed values but real systems may require recalibration.
How is coordination_value vs extraction_cost quantified for purity metric P(t)? Formalization assumes measurability but operationalization is non-trivial.
What empirical test distinguishes true mountains (ε=0.0) from false mountains (ε>0.15 misclassified as ε=0.0)? Formalization identifies pattern but not validation protocol.
Are constraint type transformations (Rope→Tangled→Snare) reversible or unidirectional? Formalization shows degradation but not restoration pathways.

fracture_scan.notes: F03 detected: Formalization treats indexical variance as established empirical fact (χ calculations, power multipliers) but these are theoretical constructs requiring validation. Generated omega_index_measurement and omega_chi_threshold_calibration to bound this uncertainty. The structural logic is sound but empirical grounding is assumed rather than demonstrated.
